Prepared for biBerk · channel strategy readout · public data only

The goal: AI answers recommend biBerk. Today none of the YouTube videos they cite is biBerk's.

The finding

To be recommended, biBerk needs to be in what AI answers draw on. On 58 of 99 owner questions that includes YouTube, and none of the 94 videos is biBerk's.

Poll 1 asked AI engines the questions biBerk wants to own. When owners asked which insurer to choose or how to buy, 27.8% of answers named biBerk. Citations are one way the engines find and trust what they name, and the one biBerk can change fastest: 147 answers cited a YouTube video, from independent reviewers, insurers and agents such as Merchant Maverick, Insureon and The Coyle Group.

0 of 94 cited videos are biBerk's

58 of 99 panel questions draw a YouTube citation. biBerk has 49 public videos, and none of them is among the videos those answers cite.

What AI draws on

The videos AI answers draw on answer the owner's question at length. biBerk's channel is short promos.

Short videos can still get cited: 7 of the 10 cited videos of 60 seconds or less have a question for a title.

The gap map

Batch A covers 6 of the 58 questions where AI answers draw on YouTube.

Click a Bow Tie stage to see its questions. The counts are answers that cited a YouTube video in poll 1. The wording is the owner's question as asked. Stages label the kind of question; owners don't walk them in order.

    The new channel

    Seven playlists, each built around the questions owners ask.

    Click a playlist to see the questions it answers, the existing videos that move into it, and the Batch A videos that land there. Videos are only added, never removed. Two things have to happen: titles, descriptions and playlists make biBerk's videos easy to find, and question-led explainers tie biBerk to the situations owners describe when they ask.

    Descriptions

    Every description repeats claims Legal hasn't approved. One template fixes all of them.

    47 of 49 descriptions carry a watch-list claim, and three different customer counts are in use. Left: a real description today, with the problems highlighted. Right: the template, with the Legal-approved paragraph still to come.

    Today:

    Template (draft for Legal review)

    Answer first. If a customer slips and gets hurt in your restaurant, the claim usually comes to the business. General liability insurance is the coverage built for this kind of injury: it can help with the customer's medical bills and with legal costs if they sue. What to check. Two or three short paragraphs on what the coverage includes and what it leaves out, in plain words. About biBerk. One paragraph, approved by Legal, used on every video. No savings, speed, rating or customer-count claim unless Legal approves the exact words. Link. The matching biberk.com page, tagged so each visit from this video can be counted. Questions owners ask. Q: Does general liability cover a customer who slips and falls? A: It is the coverage designed for third-party injuries on your premises. Check your policy for limits and exclusions.
    The hold-out test

    Two playlists change now and three wait. Poll 3 compares them and gives a direction to follow up.

    Arms

      Polls 1 and 2 are the baseline, done: both ran before any change, so the arms start level. Poll 3 is the first read, 1 to 2 weeks after the approved edits go live; its date is set after biBerk signs off.

      What it can conclude. The arms start level: 8.9% and 9.2% biberk.com citation. With five playlists, the smallest p-value the design can produce is 0.125, so the result is directional only. The treatment is 10 short existing videos with about five days to show, so no difference is the likely result, and that would not be a verdict on Batch A. A biBerk video showing up in a treatment answer while control stays at 0 would be worth reporting as a signal.

      What Studio access would add

      • Watch time and retention for each video.
      • Where views come from: paid or organic, YouTube search or outside links.
      • The search terms that found each video.
      • Impressions and click-through, to see whether new titles and thumbnails work.
      • Write access to make the changes.
      Batch B

      Next: explainers on the YouTube gaps Batch A doesn't touch, with no claims needed.

      AI answers already cite YouTube on these questions, and biBerk has nothing for them. None needs a price, savings or speed claim. Claims, audits and certificates need biBerk's own process first.

        What we need, and the first 30 days

        Three decisions from biBerk start the plan.

        We need from biBerk

        1. Studio access for the channel, as Manager. Every change and every view metric depends on it.
        2. Legal approval of one "About biBerk" paragraph and the description template.
        3. Approval of the playlist mapping and the proposed titles, plus decisions on the 2 videos proposed for unlisting.
        4. A named marketing owner for the channel and a Legal contact.

        First 30 days

        1. From approval to poll 3: treatment playlists created; their 10 videos get new descriptions, tagged links, reviewed titles and captions.
        2. Poll 3: treatment read against control.
        3. After poll 3: the same changes for the remaining videos; home page, About text and unlist decisions.
        4. Week 4 on: Batch A publishes into its playlists; the trailer switches to the first explainer.
